title: Sort Threats by Severity and Exploitability
summary: Given a 2D integer array threats with each element [ID, sevi, expi], where ID is a unique identifier, sevi represents the severity, and expi represents the exploitability.
statement: Given a 2D integer array threats with each element [ID, sevi, expi], where ID is a unique identifier, sevi represents the severity, and expi represents the exploitability. Calculate the score as score = 2 × sevi + expi. Return the threats sorted by descending score. If scores are equal, sort by ascending ID.
constraints: Each row is [unique ID, severity, exploitability].
Sort by descending score, breaking ties by ascending ID, and return all rows.
hints: Encode both ordering rules in one sort key.
Negate the score for descending order while keeping ID positive for ascending order.
Lexicographic tuple ordering applies the ID only when the primary scores tie.
editorial: Lexicographic tuple ordering applies the ID only when the primary scores tie.

tests.explanation: Scores are seven, eight, and nine, so IDs appear 103, 102, 101.
Every score is six, so the tie is ordered by IDs 1, 3, 5.
